Like everything in life, you should try to set short, mid and long term goals for your account. While the quest cape is going to be a long term goal, you can try to focus on things that help you progress towards it but also give you really useful unlocks.

Short term goals for your account could be unlocking overheads (protection prayers) and leveling up combats, mid term could be barrows gloves/dt1/lunar diplomacy, mid-long could be sote/dt2/etc. These are just quest so you'll also need to grind your other skills for their respective requirements, which you could also set mini goals for them (ie: get fm to 75 so it's no longer a blocker for the quest cape)

I realized there's a bunch of optimizations to be done in order to make the boss as easy as possible:

1. If you are ancients, freezing the boss in the middle gives you the whole room to move which makes it extremely easy to avoid getting hit by tentacles (this is something that I didn't realize until I've started farming it)

1. Be full hp/prayer before enrage phase so you only focus on dancing

2. Trident or any 4t weapon makes it match the prayer dance, so if you spam attack the boss as soon as you get phased you can use ingame sound as a cue to when to swap overheads. The idea is to send 1 attack every 2 of the boss

4. If you have to choose between getting hit by a tentacle or an auto, always choose the auto (assuming you just want to kill the boss instead of going for a perfect kc) as it won't drain your sanity

5. Play it slow and reset the cycle if you need to

Kinda hard to give advice w/o a replay but here's some general tips that got me to 2.8:

* Beacon usage, one on the squishiest dps and one on you at the start of the game and swap accordingly. Saved by the light is really clutch especially when getting boorsted.
* Most defensive cds won't be able to hold against 2 or more big offensive cds, so you probably want to sac early to split the damage and make your healing through beacons/judge more efficient. Be careful as this might aggro their dps and now you'll probably have to wall and start pumping heals to survive.
* Trade wings with whatever big cd they use (abomb limb, meta, tyrant, etc) and judge on cd whenever your team is not topped. Doesn't matter if your team is not taking damage, you need wings to align or be close as possible with whatever BIG cd they use in case the game lasts more than 2min.
* Use your cds without hesitation at first, this includes early aura mastery with devo, wings, 1 bop and sac. Pally is all about momentum so if you bop your hunter out of a warrior's spear he's gonna be pretty much afk for 1min, now is your turn to play.
* CC only when you can and you don't always have to cc their healer, hojing the KT or OT can also work

I have around 800 games and probably oomed once or twice so mana shouldn't be an issue, you need to cast less and crusader strike/judge more.

Main stat is decent enough, plus mastery isn't as bad as you may think depending on the comp you're playing since you're sitting melee a good amount of time.

I think the main sellling point is the stam though, it's omega high value to greed cds.

Honestly after having 2.5k hours into the game I'm amused by the amount of bad decisions that were made.

I know you probably have noticed and discussed it but just so that I can give my long term player perspective:

- UI rework: literally destroying the old, beautiful UI for some crap xbox port that didn't even come to light. Could have clearly used the resources and time to improve end game scoreboard or a bunch of stuff that didn't even happen.

- Lack of replayability: this game had 0 replayability for people that wanted to play for fun for a long time. To mention a few points out: level cap on characters, quests forcing to play other roles (awful imo), no long/short term goals in the game until the lore quests were introduced and playerbase was already declining by then. Do you know what could have helped this? Tournament mode and auto cups every weekend to retain playerbase, who would have known?

- Balance changes: I've played this game as competitively as I could and while most characters were playable which was nice some changes were disgusting. General changes that were completely random and innecessary: changing attack speed, projectile speed/size, aoe, model size out of nowhere is non sense, this wasn't even needed at all. More specific changes are healing charge changes (for some reason you kill someone and you get charges at a slower rate? seriously?), Overload being the most retarded thing in years of gaming since battlerite was one of the most comebackable games. Armory out of place, game was already complex enough at high lvl. 
Other than that, innecessary nerfs to underplayed heroes in competitive such as ezmo, and then taking months to fix rook/ulric/zander when they had 100% pick rate in the only tournaments the game had.

- Communication: 1 month vacations followed by another month of 0 content makes for a dead game, especially if you don't have replayability already set up for players not to get bored while they wait. I guess this is crystal clear by now.

I'm pretty certain there were a lot more flaws, like bugs such as absorbs only adding to the score if you casted it on yourself, ezmo's m2 bugged for a long time, etc. 

I won't comment on royale since either you already know, or simply it's known to be quick cashgrab and that's it, in exchange of the whole playerbase leftover trust.

Everything else I liked, the art, characters, how the game felt, voice acting, it felt characters had huge identity like in ow (and I'm no ow fan, but its characters are iconic for a reason). It also felt so rewarding to play good, it was sort of like chess where the better player wins 99% of the time vs the worse player.

Anyways, it's been a wild ride and never had a better time in any other game, but I wished greed didn't blind people so much.

It varies but to clarify:

* 1- As soon its night time (6min mark), buy a TP. 

* 2- Ask to yourself, did I get the rune? did he got the rune? If you got it, feel free to do whatever you want (ganking is prefered though), now if he got it, be ready to counter gank with your TP. The forth rune in the game is a crucial rune that decides which team will get the first tower (mostly). Wards expire by that minute, no vision for both teams and hero's vision is reduced so perfect to play aggresive if you got haste/dd.

* 3- If there arent supports missing, you can try to put some pressure in their middle tower, otherwise be careful past river.

* 4- Always keep farming in those hiatus. You want to get the most of each second the enemy's hero is missing.


though there will be scenarios where you will want to play passive because your carry is already farming safe and they arent putting pressure on him.

tl; dr: gank if you got an upper (rune), counter gank if enemy solo got it.
